text:
Casey Cizikas played his 1,000th NHL game in Detroit on Saturday, and the Islanders won it. Matthew Schaefer marked his late mother Jennifer's birthday this week, a bond NHL.com told through the ladybugs that connect them. Then Monday turned sour: a 4-2 home loss to Toronto, the Leafs' first win since Halloween, and Kyle Palmieri leaving with a lower-body injury, per Daily Faceoff.

The Islanders are 11-7-5, and by our standings model about five points better than their play. They have 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and have allowed about 13 fewer goals than those chances predict. Ilya Sorokin is the reason: a .932 save rate and 4.7 goals saved above expected over his last five starts.

Palmieri's injury hits the line that works best. He, Bo Horvat and Simon Holmstrom create 4.2 expected goals per 60 at 5-on-5 and take 58% of the chances, and Holmstrom extended his point streak to seven games; Newsday reports the Islanders think shooting more can unlock another level for him. Mathew Barzal is back from injury and picking up assists. Schaefer and Logan Stanley win 55% of the chances at 5-on-5.

Our playoff odds have New York at 39%. What we'd watch: how long Palmieri is out, and whether the shot share rises before Sorokin cools.
headline: Sorokin keeps the Islanders afloat as injuries arrive
